roster.name: Incineroar
roster.rationale: Incineroar is the most proven VGC cornerstone available: Intimidate provides immediate team-wide physical defense, Fake Out offers free turns, and Parting Shot delivers momentum-shifting speed control. Its Fire/Dark typing grants key resistances and offensive pressure, and it slots into nearly any team archetype. At 18 points it leaves 82 for nine more picks, preserving flexibility for a Mega or other high-value targets.

roster.name: Torkoal
roster.rationale: Torkoal fills three critical needs at once: Drought sun setter, natural Trick Room speed control (base 20 Speed), and a bulky physical wall (140 Def) that pairs perfectly with Incineroar's Intimidate. Sun boosts Fire moves, weakens opposing Water attacks, and synergizes with Incineroar's typing. At 15 points it leaves ample budget for a Mega anchor and remaining role fillers.

roster.name: Mega Metagross
roster.rationale: Metagross-Mega at 17 points gives me a premier offensive Mega anchor with Tough Claws, excellent Steel/Psychic typing that covers my Fire core's weaknesses to Rock, Fairy, and Ice, and strong priority in Bullet Punch. It synergizes well with Incineroar's Intimidate support and Torkoal's sun, while providing a completely different win condition from my existing Fire-type setup.

roster.name: Meowscarada
roster.rationale: Meowscarada provides 123 base Speed with Tailwind to enable my slow sun core (Torkoal/Mega Metagross), plus Grass/Dark coverage that pressures Water/Ground types threatening my Fire duo. At 12 points it leaves 38 points for 6 more picks, and Protean offers flexible typing for key matchups. This addresses my most urgent need—speed control—while adding offensive synergy.

roster.name: Mamoswine
roster.rationale: Mamoswine fills my biggest coverage gap with Ice/Ground STAB, threatening the Dragons, Flyers, and Fire-types that trouble my sun core. roster.name: Rotom-Heat

roster.name: Mega Gengar
roster.rationale: Mega Gengar is a premier draft centerpiece due to Shadow Tag, which severely restricts opponent switching and positioning in a open-sheet environment. With 170 base Special Attack and 130 Speed, it provides elite offensive coverage alongside unmatched disruptive utility through Perish Song, Disable, and Will-O-Wisp. Drafted at 18 points, it secures our primary Mega evolution while leaving a healthy 82 points across 9 picks to construct a versatile team.

roster.name: Dragonite
roster.rationale: Dragonite provides an elite physical wallbreaker and priority sweeper with Extreme Speed, perfectly balancing Mega Gengar's high special offense. Its Ground immunity and Grass/Fire/Water resistances cover Gengar's primary weaknesses, while Gengar's Shadow Tag traps and removes the Fairy, Ice, and Steel types that check Dragonite. Furthermore, Inner Focus grants immunity to Fake Out and Intimidate, giving the team an immensely reliable setup and offensive core.

roster.name: Clefable
roster.rationale: Clefable provides invaluable Follow Me redirection to preserve Dragonite's Multiscale for setups/sweeps and protect Mega Gengar's fragile physical bulk while trapping key targets with Shadow Tag. Its Fairy typing creates an exceptional defensive core with Dragonite and Mega Gengar, covering Dark and Dragon attacks while Gengar resists Poison/Fairy and Dragonite handles Ground. It also adds flexible utility with Icy Wind speed control, Helping Hand, and Unaware or Magic Guard ability options.

roster.name: Arcanine
roster.rationale: Arcanine provides crucial Intimidate and defensive pivoting to complement Mega Gengar's trapping and Clefable's redirection. Its Fire typing offers essential offensive and defensive coverage against Steel-types that threaten Clefable, while its access to Will-O-Wisp, Snarl, Flare Blitz, and Extreme Speed gives our team high utility and double priority synergy with Dragonite. At 11 points, it fits our budget comfortably, leaving 42 points across our remaining 6 picks.

roster.name: Empoleon
roster.rationale: Empoleon completes our Fairy/Dragon/Steel defensive backbone alongside Clefable and Dragonite while establishing the Water piece of our Fire/Water/Grass core with Arcanine. Its Competitive ability deters opposing Intimidate users, directly aiding Dragonite, while offering slow Flip Turn pivoting and Icy Wind speed control. At just 7 points, it fits our budget profile seamlessly while providing immunities to Poison and Sandstorm.

roster.name: Krookodile
roster.rationale: Krookodile provides a crucial Electric immunity, dark STAB coverage for opposing Ghost and Psychic types, and a fast physical Ground threat (92 Speed, 117 Attack). Its access to Intimidate stacks defensively with Arcanine, while Moxie or Anger Point builds give offensive setup options that pair naturally with Mega Gengar's trapping capability and Clefable's redirection.

roster.name: Hydrapple
roster.rationale: Hydrapple completes our Fire-Water-Grass core alongside Arcanine and Empoleon while providing excellent physical bulk and incremental speed control through Syrup Bomb. Its Grass/Dragon typing offers crucial defensive resistances to Water, Grass, Electric, and Ground moves that target our existing core. Securing Hydrapple for only 6 points leaves a healthy 20 points across our final 3 picks.

roster.name: Aerodactyl
roster.rationale: Aerodactyl provides a premier base-130 Speed Tailwind setter equipped with crucial VGC utility in Wide Guard, fast Taunt, and Rock Slide flinch pressure. Combined with Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag, Aerodactyl guarantees speed control and board lockdown against spread attackers and setup sweepers while fitting precisely within the 17-point single-pick ceiling.

roster.name: Primarina

roster.name: Raichu

draftRoster.rationale: Toxapex is gone (Sneaslers), so Gengar is the 8-cost utility piece: at 110 Speed it outspeeds Mega Floette (102) and Sludge Bomb threatens OHKOs on Clefable and Floette-Mega while deleting opposing Whimsicott, plus it brings Taunt/Will-O-Wisp/Icy Wind/Haze to cover the anti-setup role I lost with Pex. Crucially, only Aura Floettes picks before my #58 and their 4 points over 4 picks caps them at 1-cost mons, so Hippowdon (5) is guaranteed to survive until next pick — taking Gengar now costs me nothing. Gengar 8 + Hippowdon 5 leaves exactly 4 points for my two closing picks.

draftRoster.name: Hippowdon
draftRoster.rationale: Hippowdon completes my sand mode: Sand Stream doubles Excadrill's Speed via Sand Rush (154 raw → ~308, outspeeding Dragapult/M-Gengar/everything on the board), and at base 47 Speed it's slower than Pelipper/Politoed/Zard-Y, so it overwrites the rain and sun my opponents rely on (GLM, Sneaslers, Terra) whenever it switches in. It also adds a bulky Ground pivot with EQ/Rock Slide/Yawn/Whirlwind and a slow Trick Room piece next to Mimikyu. At 5 points it leaves me 4 for picks 71/74, exactly per plan.

draftRoster.name: Passimian
draftRoster.rationale: Scrafty is gone to Ironwood, so Passimian is the best 3-cost fallback and arguably better: Defiant directly punishes this league's Intimidate flood (Incineroar, both Arcanines, Staraptor, Mega Scrafty, Krookodile, Manectric), and Wide Guard shields my sand pair from opposing Rock Slide/Earthquake/Heat Wave spreads that threaten Excadrill and Blaziken. Fighting STAB also gives me a clean answer into Incineroar, Mega Scizor, Hydreigon, Farigiraf, and Snorlax, patching a coverage gap my Steel/Ground cores share. I keep 1 point back for a final utility slot.

draftRoster.name: Pikachu
draftRoster.rationale: Pikachu at 1 point fills my last slot exactly as planned: Lightning Rod redirects every Electric attack aimed at my 4x-weak Gyarados, which is huge with Rotom-Wash, Rotom-Heat, Raichu, Manectric, and Emolga scattered across opposing rosters. It also brings immediate Fake Out pressure plus Encore/Thunder Wave utility to support Kingambit and Blaziken endgames, and it can hold Light Ball to still threaten real damage despite its price.

roster.name: Mega Floette
roster.rationale: Mega Floette is the highest-upside remaining premium at 20: Fairy Aura + elite special bulk and speed make it a premier special attacker and win condition that pairs with almost any core. With the snake giving me the turnaround pick immediately after, locking this now secures a defining piece while leaving 80 points and flexibility for speed control, Intimidate/Fake Out, and weather or balance answers. Early board has already claimed several restricted roles (Incin, Whims, Gholdengo, Arch, Sneasler, CharY, Mega Gengar), so a pure Fairy powerhouse fills a clean offensive niche.

roster.name: Basculegion-Male
roster.rationale: Basculegion at 19 is the highest-value remaining attacker that immediately pairs with Mega Floette as a strong Water/Ghost Adaptability or Swift Swim physical/special threat, covering Ghost and providing Last Respects/Wave Crash pressure while the board still has rain setters and physical answers open. It avoids early Fairy overlap, fills an offensive mode need, and leaves 61 points exactly on budget for depth. Opponents have locked sun, Shadow Tag, Intimidate, Prankster Tailwind and Archaludon, so this claims a premier independent sweeper before the turnaround continues.

roster.name: Maushold
roster.rationale: Rain is dead with both Pelipper and Politoed gone, so pivot hard into glue: Maushold supplies the Follow Me redirection Farigiraf/Sinistcha would have given, Friend Guard to keep Mega Floette and Adaptability Basculegion healthy, plus Population Bomb/Wide Guard utility. At 16 it stays inside the 17-point cap and leaves 45 for seven flexible picks while contesting a piece every team wants.

roster.name: Dragapult
roster.rationale: Dragapult at 14 is the premier Tailwind setter and fast Dragon/Ghost attacker still available, pairing perfectly with Basculegion's Ghost STAB and Maushold redirection while giving my Fairy Aura core a high-speed mode and U-turn pivot. It fits the ≤17 cap cleanly and leaves 31 for six more picks focused on Intimidate, Ground, and bulk. Mega Dragonite and Annihilape remain strong backups next.

roster.name: Annihilape
roster.rationale: Annihilape at 14 is the highest-priority available piece: Fighting/Ghost coverage that pairs cleanly with Dragapult/Basculegion ghosts, Defiant into the many Intimidates still floating, and a strong physical attacker/bulk pivot our core lacks. Mega Dragonite and Aegislash are close seconds but Annihilape fills the Fighting hole more uniquely while leaving 17 for the remaining five picks. H-Arcanine remains a strong follow-up for Intimidate + Rock coverage.

roster.name: Hisuian Arcanine
roster.rationale: Hisuian Arcanine at 13 is the premier remaining Intimidate mon and fits the hard cap while adding Fire/Rock offense, utility (Will-O/Snarl/Extreme Speed), and a strong physical presence that pairs with Basculegion and Annihilape. Aegislash and Mega Dragonite exceed the 13-point ceiling, and no other ≤13 option matches the defensive speed-control and role compression Intimidate provides. Leaves exactly 4 points for four glue picks.

roster.name: Forretress
roster.rationale: Forretress is the best 1-pt glue available: Sturdy hazard setter/spinner with Volt Switch pivoting, Body Press bulk, and Steel typing that resists Fairy/Dragon while covering our complete lack of Ground answers via EQ. It rounds the offense-heavy core without overlapping roles or Fairy weakness. Remaining 1-pt slots can chase walls or Encore support next.

roster.name: Avalugg
roster.rationale: With only 1 point to spend, Avalugg is the best remaining bulk piece: 184 Def Body Press wall with Sturdy/Recover/Icy Wind gives the physical backbone and speed control the roster still lacks. It pairs cleanly with Maushold Friend Guard and Intimidate H-Arcanine while answering common physical threats (Sneasler, Kingambit, Garchomp lines) without adding another Fairy. Remaining two 1-pt picks can still chase Encore (Absol/Banette), Dark resist (G-Stunfisk), or Tailwind/Cloud Nine (Altaria).

roster.name: Absol
roster.rationale: Absol at 1pt supplies Encore plus Sucker Punch/Knock Off Dark coverage and priority that the roster lacks, pairing cleanly with Fairy Aura Floette and Ghost spam. Altaria and G-Stunfisk remain viable next for Tailwind/Cloud Nine or Dark resist, but Encore utility is the highest-leverage filler available now. Avoids Fairy overlap and spends exactly the 1pt cap.

roster.name: Galarian Stunfisk
roster.rationale: Altaria is already taken, so Galarian Stunfisk is the best remaining 1pt filler: Steel/Ground typing gives Dark and Fairy resists plus solid physical bulk and Snap Trap/Thunder Wave utility to complement Forretress hazards and Avalugg. It rounds out the defensive backbone without overlapping roles on the Fairy Aura + Adaptability + Intimidate core.

teambuilds.rationale: Opponent leans rain (Pelipper + Mega Blastoise) with Sneasler Unburden, Intimidate Tauros-Blaze, Toxapex, and bulky support. Bring Mega Floette Fairy Aura offense, rain-abusing Basculegion, Friend Guard Maushold redirection, Dragapult speed/ghost pressure, Intimidate H-Arcanine for physical checks and Fire coverage, and Annihilape for Rage Fist bulk vs their physicals. Outspeed and pressure Sneasler/Manectric, break Toxapex/Snorlax with Aura + Adaptability, and use Intim/FG to blunt Tauros and Sneasler while Floette and Pult clean.

We bring Mega Gengar, Krookodile, Aerodactyl, Dragonite, Arcanine, and Hydrapple to exert strong offensive pressure, speed control, and Intimidate support against DeepSeek's roster. Fast Tailwind from Aerodactyl coupled with Scarf/Fast Ground and Dark moves from Krookodile and Gengar pressures key threats like Gholdengo, Hydreigon, and Rotom-Wash. Double Intimidate and Hydrapple's bulk check physical threats like Mudsdale and Azumarill.

We bring a powerful anti-meta composition designed to control speed, shut down sand/spread damage, and neutralize physical sweepers like Mega Blaziken, Kingambit, and Excadrill. Aerodactyl provides crucial speed control via Tailwind and neutralizes Excadrill/Hippowdon spread moves with Wide Guard while preventing Prankster Whimsicott setups via Taunt. Mega Gengar traps key targets with Shadow Tag, threatening Fairy/Grass types with STAB Sludge Bomb and burning physical attackers with Will-O-Wisp, while Arcanine and Clefable provide Intimidate, follow-me redirection, and status mitigation. Empoleon punishes Gyarados's Intimidate with Competitive while holding Shuca Berry to survive Ground hits, and Dragonite serves as a versatile, resilient physical cleaner.

Lead Mega Charizard Y with Raichu or Talonflame to establish sun while denying Politoed, Grimmsnarl, or Noivern their first disruptive turn. Chlorophyll Venusaur punishes the rain mode and outruns their entire roster in sun, while Garchomp and Hisuian Goodra give redundant answers to Archaludon and Mega Scizor. Talonflame is the backup speed-control and Serperior check, with Mental Herb specifically preserving Tailwind through Taunt.

Mega Charizard Y plus Chlorophyll Venusaur is the primary mode: Drought removes Pelipper rain, enables immediate Solar Beam, and lets Venusaur outspeed the opposing roster outside of unusual boosts. Raichu denies Pelipper/Manectric Electric pressure while supplying Fake Out and speed control; Primarina and Hisuian Goodra cover the Water-heavy Mega Blastoise mode, while Garchomp pressures Manectric, Toxapex, and Tauros. If Cloud Nine Altaria appears, prioritize removing it with Primarina or Goodra before committing to the sun endgame.

Rain core (Politoed Drizzle + Archaludon Electro Shot + Noivern Hurricane) overrides Mega Charizard Y's Drought and lets Archaludon fire one-turn Electro Shot for SE hits on Zard-Y/Talonflame. Garganacl provides Wide Guard to block Garchomp Earthquake and Zard-Y Heat Wave spread while Rock Slide quad-hits Talonflame. Grimmsnarl adds Prankster dual screens + Fake Out + Spirit Break for Garchomp. Mega Scizor cleans late with Technician Bullet Punch priority. Noivern at 192 Spe outspeeds most of the meta except max-Speed Talonflame.

Opponent leans sun (Torkoal) + Mega Metagross Tough Claws with Incineroar Intimidate/Fake Out, Meowscarada, and Mamoswine as primary wincons. We answer with Fairy Aura Mega Floette plus Friend Guard Maushold redirection, Rock Head H-Arcanine Head Smash/Blitz, and a Ghost trio (Dragapult/Annihilape/Basculegion) that pressures Metagross, Hatterene, and Incin while Wave Crash covers Torkoal/Mamoswine. Open team sheets favor hard-hitting STAB and clear speed tiers; no weather of our own, just out-offense and chip through FG/redirect.

The opponent's roster features Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag, 170 SpA, 130 Spe), Dragonite (Multiscale), and fast threats like Aerodactyl, Arcanine, and Krookodile. This team answers with a Trick Room core: Farigiraf sets TR and blocks priority with Armor Tail, Gholdengo threatens with Make It Rain and Shadow Ball, and Azumarill, Gliscor, and Rotom-Wash become devastating under TR. Hydreigon provides a mixed-speed option with Earth Power for opposing Steel-types. Will-O-Wisp from Rotom-Wash cripples physical attackers, Ice Fang from Gliscor handles Hydrapple and Dragonite, and Azumarill's Play Rough breaks Multiscale and threatens Hydrapple. Focus Sash Gholdengo ensures it survives Gengar's Shadow Ball to retaliate, while Farigiraf's Mental Herb blocks Taunt from Gengar.

The opponent's key threats are Mega Scizor (Technician priority), Archaludon (Stamina bulk), Noivern/Serperior (high speed), and Garganacl (bulky Salt Cure). Farigiraf's Armor Tail shuts down all priority from Scizor, Grimmsnarl, and Staraptor, while Trick Room reverses their speed advantage. Under Trick Room, Mudsdale (Stamina-boosted Body Press and Heavy Slam) and Gholdengo (Life Orb) become devastating breakers. Hydreigon with Choice Scarf provides emergency speed control and Fire/Ground coverage for Scizor/Archaludon/Garganacl. Rotom-Wash burns physical attackers and checks rain. Azumarill with Expert Belt + Huge Power gives priority Aqua Jet and Fairy coverage for Dragons and Darks.

Sun + Intimidate core weakens physical threats like Dragapult and Annihilape while boosting our Fire coverage. Mega Metagross handles Fairy and Ice types, Meowscarada and Rotom-Heat apply fast special pressure, and Mamoswine's Ice Shard cleans up faster Dragons and Normal types. Torkoal sets sun to empower Fire moves and weaken Water attacks, while Incineroar provides crucial pivoting and Intimidate support.

Rain core of Politoed+Archaludon+Noivern exploits the opponent's lack of a Water resist and gives Archaludon instant Electro Shot to shred Corviknight/Rotom-Wash. Grimmsnarl's Prankster Reflect+Play Rough answers Hydreigon (4x SE OHKO) while Fake Out provides flinch support. Mega Scizor walls Azumarill (Play Rough does 5-11%) and cleans with Technician Bullet Punch. Staraptor's Intimidate+Final Gambit removes a key threat at 167 Spe, outspeeding everything but Hydreigon on their roster. Noivern at 192 Spe is the fastest thing on the field, OHKOing Hydreigon with Draco Meteor and chunking Trevenant/Gliscor with rain-boosted Hurricane.

This six counters Moonshot's physical-heavy roster with double Intimidate pressure, Magic Bounce to shut down Whimsicott's Prankster, and sun to weaken their Water/Fire coverage while powering Torkoal's Heat Wave. Mega Metagross is the primary win condition under sun or Trick Room, with Meowscarada's always-crit Flower Trick pressuring Gyarados, Hippowdon, and Passimian. Mamoswine's Ice Shard picks off weakened Gyarados and Gengar. Hatterene's Magic Bounce + Trick Room gives us a secondary speed-control mode when Tailwind or Prankster disrupts our natural pace.

Opponent runs rain-abusing Basculegion (Swift Swim), fast Dragapult, Mega Floette Fairy spammer, Annihilape, and Hisuian Arcanine. I lead rain mode with Pelipper + Mega Blastoise to wallbreak Basculegion/Forretress/Avalugg and outpace under drizzle. Toxapex special-walls Dragapult and Basculegion with Regenerator; Chilling Water drops physical attackers' Atk. Houndoom pivots in on Arcanine (Flash Fire) and threatens Dragapult/Annihilape with Dark Pulse. Sneasler Unburden-sweeps after White Herb, outspeeding Dragapult to revenge-kill. Altaria provides Ground immunity pivot and Draco Meteor for Dragons, with Charti Berry softening Arcanine Rock coverage.

Opponent runs sun mode with Mega Charizard Y (Drought), Venusaur (Chlorophyll), and Talonflame (Gale Wings priority). Drought overrides my rain, so I pivot around it: Houndoom's Flash Fire absorbs Fire moves and threatens back with Fire/Dark STAB boosted by Charcoal; Manectric's Lightning Rod pivots in on Raichu/Emolga and Choice Scarf outspeeds the field; Pelipper still sets rain if Charizard Y faints and provides Wide Guard against Heat Wave; Sneasler uses White Herb to trigger Unburden and sweep with Close Combat/Acrobatics; Sinistcha sets Trick Room for Snorlax's Curse sweep under rain or post-sun.

openrouter's board is heavily physical (Dragonite, Arcanine, Krookodile, Aerodactyl, Morpeko), so Gyarados Intimidate plus Hippowdon sand chip is premium — and sand also breaks Dragonite's Multiscale. Sand Rush Excadrill hits effective 280 Speed, outrunning both of their 130-base threats (Mega Gengar, Aerodactyl), and Earthquake/Iron Head/Rock Slide land super-effectively on 7 of their 10 mons. Mega Gengar is walled by Kingambit (Shadow Ball does 19-27%) and deleted by Black Glasses Sucker Punch, while Whimsicott provides Prankster Tailwind/Encore/Taunt as the non-sand speed control and anti-setup layer. Mega Blaziken is the breaker: CC removes Krookodile/Empoleon, Brave Bird 2HKOs Hydrapple, and one Speed Boost puts it past their entire roster.

Rain mode with Pelipper + Mega Blastoise to overwrite Torkoal's sun and boost Water moves. Houndoom (Flash Fire, Choice Scarf) absorbs Fire moves from Torkoal/Incineroar/Rotom-Heat and revenge kills mid-speed threats. Toxapex (Regenerator) walls special attackers like Rotom-Heat, Meowscarada, and Hatterene. Sneasler (Unburden + White Herb) is the late-game cleaner, outspeeding everything after Close Combat triggers the speed boost. Altaria provides Ground immunity pivot against Mamoswine/Scrafty Earthquakes.

This team leverages Sun + Intimidate to neutralize the opponent's physical threats (Sneasler, Tauros, Snorlax) while Mega Metagross and Meowscarada provide overwhelming offensive pressure. Torkoal's Drought shuts down Pelipper's rain and powers up Fire moves, while Mamoswine's Ice Shard picks off fast Dragon/Flying types like Altaria and Manectric. Rotom-Heat covers Water and Flying types with Levitate and strong special attacks, and Incineroar provides crucial Fake Out support and pivoting.

Opponent's Whimsicott Prankster, Kingambit Sucker Punch, and Mimikyu priority are all shut down by Farigiraf's Armor Tail, making it the lynchpin of the matchup. Farigiraf sets Trick Room to turn Blaziken's Speed Boost and Excadrill's Sand Rush into liabilities. Gholdengo's Good as Gold blocks status moves from Whimsicott and Gengar while sweeping with Nasty Plot. Rotom-Wash burns physical threats (Blaziken, Kingambit, Excadrill) and hits the Water-weak Hippowdon/Excadrill hard. Azumarill Belly Drums under Trick Room to clean. Mudsdale walls Kingambit with Stamina and OHKOs Mimikyu with Heavy Slam. Hydreigon gives a fast revenge option outside Trick Room, hitting Gengar and Excadrill super-effectively. The six cover all of opponent's likely cores while Armor Tail eliminates their speed advantage strategies.

GLM’s core threats are rain Politoed, Mega Scizor, Stamina Archaludon, Prankster Grimm screens, Contrary Serperior, and fat Dark/Rock walls. Bring Fairy Aura Mega Floette as the neutral-offense wincon, Intimidate H-Arcanine to delete Mega Scizor and check Staraptor/Serperior, Annihilape to bust Umbreon/Garganacl, Dragapult as the speed tier that outruns Noivern/Serperior with utility, Maushold Friend Guard + Follow Me to escort Floette, and Swift Swim Basculegion to steal drizzle and snowball Last Respects.

Rain core of Politoed+Archaludon+Noivern punishes the opponent's Fire/Rock (Hisuian Arcanine) and gives Noivern perfect Hurricanes. Staraptor provides Intimidate to cut Annihilape/Dragapult physical damage and Final Gambit to remove any key threat at 192 HP. Grimmsnarl gives Prankster screens + Fake Out + Taunt to slow Mega Floette and stop setup. Mega Scizor Bullet Punch is the priority cleaner that OHKOs or heavily chunks Mega Floette (2x Steel SE) and revenge-kills weakened Dragapult/Annihilape. Archaludon Electro Shot in rain one-shots Basculegion and chunks Forretress/Stunfisk while Draco Meteor handles Dragapult.

Against their sun-and-dragon offense (Mega Charizard Y, Venusaur, Garchomp, Talonflame, Raichu), Aerodactyl's fast Wide Guard completely shuts down Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Garchomp's Earthquake while OHKOing both Fire/Flyings with Rock Slide. Mega Gengar uses Shadow Tag to trap and remove high-value targets like Primarina or Venusaur, while Inner Focus Dragonite ignores Raichu's Fake Out to land 4x effective moves on Garchomp and Charizard Y. Arcanine and Krookodile combine Intimidate support and Choice Scarf speed control to suppress physical threats, with Clefable providing Follow Me redirection for smooth endgame setups.

Mega Charizard Y plus Chlorophyll Venusaur is the primary mode: sun makes Venusaur faster than Mega Gengar and Aerodactyl while Charizard pressures Gengar, Clefable, and Empoleon immediately. Choice Scarf Garchomp supplies a second anti-speed-control option and strong Rock/Ground coverage, while Primarina and Hisuian Goodra cover Dragonite, Krookodile, Hydrapple, and special attackers. Talonflame gives priority Tailwind and Taunt insurance against opposing Tailwind or Trick Room lines.

The opponent's core threats are Mega Metagross (Tough Claws, 110 Spe) and Hatterene (Magic Bounce, TR). Gholdengo with Life Orb OHKOs both with Shadow Ball, while Good as Gold blocks status. Farigiraf uses Imprison to deny Hatterene's Trick Room or sets its own, and Armor Tail blocks Fake Out / priority. Hydreigon with Choice Scarf outspeeds Meowscarada and Metagross, hitting them with Heat Wave / Earth Power. Azumarill Belly Drums behind Sitrus Berry to threaten Incineroar, Torkoal, and Mamoswine with Aqua Jet. Corviknight walls Meowscarada completely (Flower Trick does ~5%) and provides Tailwind speed control, while Mirror Armor punishes Intimidate. Gliscor with Hyper Cutter ignores Intimidate and hits Metagross / Incineroar / Torkoal with Earthquake.

The opponent likely brings Politoed for rain, Mega Scizor as a top threat, Serperior as a Contrary sweeper, Archaludon as a bulky special attacker, and Staraptor for Intimidate. My rain core (Pelipper + Mega Blastoise) matches their weather, with Blastoise's Mega Launcher boosting Hydro Pump to 3.375x in rain. Houndoom and Tauros-Blaze provide Fire coverage to handle Scizor (Fire is 2x). Sneasler uses Unburden + White Herb to outspeed Serperior and Staraptor after Intimidate triggers, hitting Archaludon with Close Combat and Staraptor with Rock Slide. Toxapex walls special attackers like Serperior and Archaludon with Regenerator and can Haze away Contrary boosts.

DeepSeek's Gholdengo/Farigiraf stack folds to my note's answer: Gengar + Kingambit + Mold Breaker Excadrill. Excadrill (Jolly 154) edges max-speed Gholdengo (149) and Rotom (151), and Mold Breaker lets High Horsepower hit Rotom-W/Hydreigon through Levitate — both take 85-166%. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave OHKO-range's both Gholdengo (84-150%) and Farigiraf (79-145%), with Sucker Punch cleaned up by Armor Tail awareness. Whimsicott (184) and Gengar (178) outrun max-speed Hydreigon (165) and delete it with 4x Fairy moves; Gyarados Intimidates Azumarill/Mudsdale/Mawile, walls Gliscor completely, and 4x Ice Fang removes it; Mega Blaziken Speed Boost snowballs through their Steel stack (Gholdengo, Corviknight, Mawile, Trevenant) and even tanks Azumarill's Play Rough since Fairy is resisted by Fire here. Tailwind also turns Kingambit (70->140) into a mid-speed sweeper over their slow halves.

Rain core of Politoed+Archaludon+Noivern exploits the opponent's Water-types (Pelipper 4x, Mega Blastoise 2x to Electro Shot) while Noivern at 192 Spe outspeeds Sneasler's 189 and OHKOs with rain Hurricane. Grimmsnarl provides Prankster dual screens (Reflect+Light Screen) and Fake Out support to mitigate both physical and special damage. Staraptor with Focus Sash is the emergency Sneasler answer via Intimidate+Brave Bird or Final Gambit to remove any key threat. Mega Scizor cleans with Technician Bullet Punch priority and Close Combats Snorlax/Toxapex. Archaludon's Stamina makes it progressively tankier against physical hits, and Earthquake handles Toxapex.

This opponent leans on bulky Steel/Ghost (Gholdengo), Water/Fairy (Azumarill), and Flying/Steel (Corviknight) cores backed by setup and speed control. We counter with Sun + Trick Room duality to dictate pace, Intimidate pivots to soften physical threats like Mudsdale and Mawile, and Mega Metagross as a resilient Steel anchor. Meowscarada's guaranteed-crit Flower Trick shreds Azumarill and Rotom-Wash, while Hatterene's 4x Fairy coverage deletes Hydreigon and bounces status. Mamoswine provides crucial Ice priority and Ground coverage for Gholdengo and Gliscor, ensuring we break through their defensive walls.

Mega Charizard Y plus Chlorophyll Venusaur is the primary mode: sun denies Hippowdon sand, threatens Kingambit/Excadrill, and lets Venusaur outrun the opposing roster for Sleep Powder or direct pressure. Rain core (Pelipper + Mega Blastoise) blasts through the opponent's water-weak team with Water Spout, Hydro Pump, and Ice Beam. Snorlax is immune to Gengar's Shadow Ball, walls physical attackers with Thick Fat, and sweeps with Curse. Tauros-Blaze provides Intimidate to weaken physical threats like Krookodile, Aerodactyl, and Dragonite. Toxapex walls Empoleon and other special attackers, sets Toxic Spikes, and shuts down setup sweepers like Clefable with Haze.

Rain core (Pelipper Drizzle + Mega Blastoise Water Spout) disables Excadrill's Sand Rush and weakens Mega Blaziken's Fire STAB while powering up Water Spout. Sneasler uses Sitrus Berry Unburden to threaten Kingambit with 4x SE Close Combat and OHKO Mega Blaziken. Houndoom's Flash Fire lets it pivot into Blaziken's (rain-weakened) Fire for free, then Nasty Plot wallbreaks. Manectric provides Lightning Rod pivot and Volt Switch momentum, with Overheat for Whimsicott/Mimikyu. Altaria is the Ground-immunity tank that switches into Excadrill/Hippowdon Earthquakes and Roosts back up.

Rain core of Politoed+Archaludon+Noivern punishes the opponent's likely sun (Torkoal) by overriding with Drizzle, while Archaludon Electro Shot sweeps under rain and Noivern outspeeds everything (192 Spe) with perfect-accuracy Hurricane to nuke Meowscarada/Scrafty. Grimmsnarl provides Prankster screens+Fake Out to protect the setup turn, Mega Scizor Bullet Punch cleans weakened targets (SE on Hatterene/Mamoswine), and Garganacl's Purifying Salt+Wide Guard walls Metagross Rock Slide and spreads Salt Cure chip on the Steel-types. Key speed tiers: Noivern 192 outruns Meowscarada 123 and Dedenne 101; Archaludon 123 ties base 120s; Scizor priority bypasses all speed ties.

Rain core of Politoed+Archaludon+Noivern punishes the opponent's Fire-weak Blaziken-Mega and Water/Flying Gyarados (4x Electro Shot). Grimmsnarl provides Prankster Reflect+Fake Out+Parting Shot to slow Mega Blaziken and Excadrill while Staraptor's Intimidate+Final Gambit+Tailwind handles speed control and removes key threats at 167 Spe. Mega Scizor is the bulky priority cleaner and Kingambit check with Close Combat, while Archaludon's Aura Sphere hits Kingambit 4x SE.

Rain core of Politoed+Archaludon+Noivern punishes the opponent's Fire-types (Arcanine) and lets Archaludon fire Electro Shot in one turn while Noivern gets perfect Hurricanes. Grimmsnarl provides Prankster dual screens + Fake Out + Taunt to shut down Dragonite/Clefable setup and buffer against Mega Gengar's special nukes. Staraptor's Intimidate stacks against their Arcanine/Krookodile Intimidate and Final Gambit from 192 HP can remove Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag) or a boosted Dragonite. Mega Scizor is the bulky priority cleaner with Bullet Punch and U-turn to pivot around Shadow Tag trapping.

The opponent's biggest threat is Gholdengo (133 SpA, Good as Gold blocks status), supported by fast special attackers (Hydreigon, Rotom-Wash, Farigiraf) and heavy physical attackers (Azumarill/Mawile Huge Power, Mudsdale, Gliscor, Corviknight). I bring rain mode (Pelipper Drizzle + Mega Blastoise) to crush Mudsdale/Gliscor/Azumarill/Rotom-Wash with rain-boosted Water spam, Houndoom as the dedicated Gholdengo answer (Flash Fire immune to its only weakness, Fire Blast/Dark Pulse both 2x SE), Manectric with Lightning Rod to pivot on Rotom-Wash and threaten Azumarill/Corviknight with Electric, Sinistcha for Grass/Ghost coverage on Azumarill/Rotom-Wash/Farigiraf plus Hospitality team healing, and Tauros-Blaze with Intimidate to soften the many physical attackers while hitting Gholdengo/Corviknight/Mawile/Trevenant with Flare Blitz.

The opponent has a strong rain core (Pelipper + Blastoise-Mega), fast threats (Sneasler, Tauros, Manectric) and bulky pivots (Toxapex, Sinistcha). I answer with Gholdengo (status immunity, Fighting immunity to Aura Sphere), Rotom-Wash (rain check, Will-O-Wisp), Gliscor (Sneasler/Tauros check via Fighting immunity + Focus Sash), Corviknight (physical wall + Tailwind speed control), Choice Scarf Hydreigon (revenge kills Unburden Sneasler with Scarf Dark Pulse, hits Sinistcha and Toxapex), and Farigiraf (Armor Tail blocks priority Sucker Punch/Aqua Jet, Trick Room reverses speed). Lead Farigiraf+Gliscor or Rotom-Wash+Gholdengo depending on preview; use Tailwind or Trick Room to control the pace.

Lead Pelipper and Mega Blastoise to establish rain and pressure Excadrill, Hippowdon, Gyarados, and Blaziken with spread Water attacks while Wide Guard and Icy Wind control opposing spread damage and speed. Sneasler provides fast disruption and strong Fighting pressure into Kingambit, Mimikyu, and Passimian, while Tauros-Blaze checks Steel types and benefits from Intimidate. Sinistcha is the defensive anti-physical option with Rage Powder, Trick Room, and recovery, giving the team a mode against Speed Boost Blaziken and sand teams.

Mega Gengar traps key targets with Shadow Tag, neutralizing setup and burning physical threats while threatening fast KO attacks. Unaware Clefable completely ignores Contrary Leaf Storm boosts from Serperior and Stamina defense boosts from Archaludon. Aerodactyl provides fast Tailwind, Wide Guard to block spread attacks like Muddy Water/Rock Slide/Hyper Voice, and Taunt. Scarf Krookodile and Intimidate Arcanine pressure Archaludon and Scizor, while Competitive Empoleon discourages Staraptor's Intimidate and provides high SpA coverage.

Opponent's physical core (Mega Blaziken Speed Boost, Kingambit, Gyarados, Excadrill + Hippowdon sand) plus Prankster Whimsicott and Mimikyu/Gengar is answered by Intimidate H-Arcanine, Fairy Aura Mega Floette, Adaptability Basculegion Wave Crash/Aqua Jet, and Annihilape Close Combat (4x Kingambit) + Rage Fist. Dragapult Scarf provides speed control and Ghost pressure through Disguise; Maushold Friend Guard + Follow Me/Population Bomb supports and chips. Balanced Intim/FG offense over hazards.

Rain core (Politoed+Archaludon+Noivern) overrides the opponent's Hippowdon sand, neutering Sand Rush Excadrill and weakening Mega Blaziken's Fire moves to trivial damage on Archaludon. Grimmsnarl's Dark typing makes it immune to Whimsicott's Prankster moves while providing screens and Fake Out; Noivern at 192 Spe outspeeds Gengar and Taunts Whimsicott. Mega Scizor's Bullet Punch picks off weakened targets and Close Combat OHKOs Kingambit, while Scarf Staraptor outspeeds everything for Final Gambit removal of any threat.

Mega Metagross and Incineroar form a defensive core that hard walls Archaludon and Scizor-Mega while applying heavy pressure. Mamoswine's Ice Shard and High Horsepower clean up Flying/Dragon types and break through Archaludon/Garganacl. Meowscarada outspeeds and eliminates Politoed, Serperior, and Umbreon with Flower Trick. Hatterene's Magic Bounce shuts down Grimmsnarl's Prankster support, while Torkoal's Drought neutralizes Rain and powers up Eruption/Heat Wave.

Rain core of Politoed + Archaludon + Noivern handles the opponent's Fire/Water/Grass/Dragon threats, with Grimmsnarl providing Prankster screens + Fake Out to break Dragonite's Multiscale for Noivern's Draco Meteor. Staraptor's Intimidate stacks vs their physical attackers (Krookodile, Dragonite, Arcanine, Aerodactyl) while Close Combat and Final Gambit give emergency answers. Mega Scizor's Bullet Punch priority picks off weakened Gengar and Clefable, and Close Combat OHKOs Krookodile. Under Tailwind from Noivern, the whole team outspeeds Gengar-Mega's 130 base Spe, letting Archaludon's Life Orb Electro Shot potentially OHKO Gengar in rain.

Rain core (Politoed+Archaludon+Noivern) overrides Torkoal sun and neuters Fire damage from Incineroar/Rotom-Heat. Archaludon quad-resists Metagross Steel STAB and survives its Earthquake (28-49%), hitting back with SE Earthquake; Mega Scizor walls Metagross's Steel attacks (13-23% per hit) and provides Bullet Punch priority that 2HKO Hatterene. Noivern (192 Spe) speed-ties Meowscarada and OHKOs with rain Hurricane; Super Fang halves Metagross/Hatterene for partner cleanup. Staraptor adds Intimidate stack, Brave Bird for Meowscarada/Mamoswine, Close Combat for Incineroar, and Final Gambit to remove any boosted threat. Grimmsnarl provides Prankster screens + Fake Out for team bulk and tempo.

Mega Charizard Y plus Venusaur is the primary sun mode: Drought overwrites Politoed rain, turns off immediate Electro Shot, and gives Chlorophyll Venusaur the speed advantage over Noivern and Serperior. Talonflame prevents Grimmsnarl disruption and supplies Tailwind insurance, while Raichu adds Fake Out, paralysis, and Lightning Rod protection. Garchomp is the direct Archaludon answer, and Hisuian Goodra gives a durable Serperior-resistant special pivot with Fire coverage for Mega Scizor.

Against DeepSeek Gholdengos' core of Farigiraf Trick Room, Gholdengo spread pressure, and Azumarill/Rotom-W/Hydreigon offensive backbones, we bring a proven fast disruptor and double Intimidate package. Aerodactyl provides fast Taunt to shut down Trick Room setup and Wide Guard to block Gholdengo's Make It Rain and Ground spread moves. Scarf Krookodile and Mega Gengar exert intense offensive pressure on Gholdengo and Farigiraf, trapping and KOing key threats, while Arcanine, Dragonite, and Hydrapple form a durable pivot core that walls and neutralizes Azumarill, Rotom-Wash, and Mudsdale.

This rematch demands answers to Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag, 170 SpA, 130 Spe) and Dragonite (Multiscale). Gholdengo's Ghost typing makes it immune to Shadow Tag, and Focus Sash guarantees it survives Gengar's Shadow Ball to retaliate with Shadow Ball. Choice Scarf Hydreigon outspeeds and threatens Gengar with Dark Pulse, and hits Dragonite with Draco Meteor after Multiscale is broken. Farigiraf sets Trick Room to reverse their speed advantage while Armor Tail blocks priority from Dragonite's Extreme Speed and Krookodile's Sucker Punch. Azumarill's Huge Power Play Rough breaks Multiscale and threatens Hydrapple; Rotom-Wash spreads burns to cripple Arcanine and Krookodile; and Mudsdale's Stamina-boosted Body Press and Earthquake clean up under Trick Room. Lead Gholdengo + Hydreigon to pressure the likely Dragonite+Gengar lead.

Rain core (Politoed+Archaludon+Noivern) overrides Mega Charizard-Y's Drought, neutering Fire damage and enabling Archaludon's one-turn Electro Shot; Life Orb Draco Meteor guaranteed OHKOs Garchomp. Garganacl walls Charizard-Y under rain (Flamethrower 6-20%), Wide Guard blocks Garchomp EQ and Zard-Y Heat Wave spread, while Rock Slide quad-hits Zard-Y/Talonflame. Grimmsnarl's Prankster screens + Fake Out provide bulk and tempo, Spirit Break chunks Garchomp. Staraptor's Intimidate + Brave Bird OHKOs Venusaur, Close Combat threatens Goodra-Hisui, Final Gambit is emergency nuke. Noivern at 192 Spe outspeeds everything but Talonflame, threatening Hurricane on Venusaur and Draco Meteor on Garchomp. Mega Scizor benched (4x Fire weak, liability vs sun).

Against Terra Solar Wings' sun-and-dragon offense, Aerodactyl provides crucial speed control via Tailwind and completely shuts down Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Garchomp's Earthquake with Wide Guard while Rock Slide threatens their Fire/Flying threats. Inner Focus Dragonite ignores Raichu's Fake Out to land 4x effective Ice Spinner on Garchomp and heavy Rock Slide damage. Mega Gengar traps key targets like Primarina and Venusaur with Shadow Tag, while double Intimidate from Choice Scarf Krookodile and Arcanine suppresses physical threats and Clefable provides redirection.

Use Choice Scarf Garchomp as the immediate anti-Mega-Gengar and anti-Aerodactyl speed piece; its 253 effective Speed outruns both even at maximum investment, and Ground coverage cleanly threatens Gengar. Primarina is the crucial Dragonite, Krookodile, and Arcanine answer, while Hisuian Goodra gives a resilient special pivot into Gengar, Hydrapple, Empoleon, and Clefable. Mega Charizard Y and Focus Sash Venusaur remain the sun mode, but avoid leaving Charizard exposed as the sole endgame answer against Aerodactyl or Dragonite.
